source: Hand-tuned for gameplay; categories modeled on common NASA science instrument types

rows: A small color camera. Takes pictures of Earth from orbit.
Measures magnetic fields. Tiny, cheap, always on.
Counts high-energy particles. More interesting the farther you are from Earth's protective magnetic field.
Splits light into colors to find what things are made of: minerals, gases, ice.
Measures temperature and moisture through the atmosphere. Weather forecasters love these.
Fires laser pulses at the ground to map its height, perfect for mapping the Moon.
A high-resolution camera that sees colors humans can't, used for crops, forests and water.
Sends radio pulses deep into the ground to find buried ice. Works best on Mars.
Watches one whole side of Earth nonstop. Tracks storms as they form.
Looks at hot young stars and galaxies in light our atmosphere blocks.
Sees through clouds and darkness by bouncing radio waves off the ground. Power hungry!
